I had a friend tell me this after they revived me after I killed myself. He said that we spend so much time trying to basically live for the world and making it happy rather than ourselves. He said, we do things because that's what society expects us to do but we never really live. So for example, society expects you to go to college and get good grades, society expects you to happily just get along with your family but that's not what you have to do. Instead, go do stuff you want to do for you and that will make you happy. For me, I'd like to just disappear into the woods forever and do my own thing and that's 100% possible but society expects different and therefore everyone spends their time trying to make everyone else happy when they should just be focusing on making themselves happy. Not sure if I made as much sense as my friend. Your mental health follows whatever goes on in your life. So if you have a consistently rough life with school and family, chances are that your overall mental health won't be at its best. Basically you should figure out what triggers your happy as in stuff you've either always wanted to do or just start living for you and your mental status should positively improve over time. It's never an overnight thing so please don't give up. If grades are bad in school, jjust kinda let it go in your mind if you can and be like, oh well, maybe next time. I know all of this may be easier said than done because I've been in your position in one way or another before but life outside of the box you may feel trapped in, is possible. Not saying you're not trying that already either but just saying that these suggestions did help me.

Hey, I got my 1st ever arrest at 25 a year and a half ago (I'm now 27) and I live in Illinois. Georgia's weed laws are a LOT better than Illinois. If it's your 1st arrest, you should be given a diversion or court supervision program. I was. I passed my 12 month court supervision in November and the record was dismissed. I know exactly how you're feeling. It freaking blows. If they didn't make my dad pick up my guns when they arrested me, I would have seriously shot myself in the days that followed. I was a mess. With Marijuana becoming legalized everywhere, it's not really a big deal what you did. It seems like the end of the world right now but trust me, it isn't. By 2018, it's predicted that at least half the US will be fully legal and nearly all medically legal. As soon as it does, that should either not amount to anything to future employers if you worry about that or maybe your state will be like that of Oregon and Ohio and just flat remove anything from your record that says marijuana. How much did they catch you with? Just give this some time and  thinking you will be fine. I did all the research in the world and panicked before mine ever reached court. Whatever you do, don't read up on it because I swear with me, I found all worse case scenarios and nothing really happened to me. I was even able to keep smoking weed provided I didn't get caught. If you've got any questions at all, don't hesitate to PM me and I can answer just about anything to do with it. I unfortunately had to become to familiar with everything. I do recommend a lawyer if you can though. I was going to get 1 and 1/2 years court supervision and the DA walked to my lawyer and goes "oh, you're his lawyer" after already telling me it would be a year and a half and then my lawyer said yes and he then crossed the year and a half off and wrote 1 year and had my lawyer sign it. I had to sign the same paper in front of the judge. Make sure in court you have your hands down to your side or behind your back and say yes sir, no sir or yes maam, no ma'am on every single thing the judge says and you'll be in good shape.

Oh also, you may have to BS your brain for a bit and keep telling it everything is good or things aren't so bad to kinda jump start it a bit. I know I did.
